statements.status_notes: The SQLite disclosure requires opening a database together with a crafted sibling WAL file. InfluxDB 3 Core 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12 use SQLx only for data_types type and codec implementations, with no SQLite connection or database-open path. The published amd64 and arm64 Core binaries, identical between runtime and dev variants, have no sqlite3_open, sqlite3_open_v2 or sqlite3WalReadFrame symbols. Python's separate _sqlite3 extension links the distro SQLite library, not this Cargo component. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0459.html and the upstream assessment at https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb/blob/51f4ac865b8670e0d3555ae992639ec05ecc334e/deny.toml

The published amd64 and arm64 Core binaries, identical between runtime and dev variants, have no sqlite3_open, sqlite3_open_v2 or sqlite3WalReadFrame symbols. Python's separate _sqlite3 extension links the distro SQLite library, not this Cargo component. See https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0459.html and the upstream assessment at https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb/blob/51f4ac865b8670e0d3555ae992639ec05ecc334e/deny.toml

CVE-2026-119375 is an information disclosure in SQLite before 3.54.0 when a database is opened with a crafted WAL file. libsqlite3-sys is the Rust binding crate for SQLite and appears in the SBOM because the Cargo.lock of flux v0.201.0 lists it, but it is not compiled into Kapacitor. Its only dependent in the lock file is rusqlite, which flux-core declares as an optional dependency that only the analyze_query_log helper binary requires through required-features, and no flux-core feature that Kapacitor builds enables it. Kapacitor builds libflux with `cargo build --release --no-default-features --features=cffi`, and flux v0.201.0 depends on flux-core with default-features = false, so rusqlite is not built. The amd64 kapacitord binary contains no symbols from the rusqlite or libsqlite3_sys crate, while the crates that are compiled in (anyhow, chrono, libflate, parking_lot_core) do.
